text: Attempt 19: attempt 17's mixed layout with LIGHT homes (17 and 18 both stopped near 29,000 with dense homes outrunning jobs), more factory cells, the second seaport at ~20,000, and population reminders that stop the loop so no planned step is missed.
Day one, light homes (a11-day1).
Attempts 17 and 18 hit the same ~29,000 plateau with unemployment 11-14% and hundreds of empty dense homes. Attempt 19 goes back to light homes inside the mixed layout so jobs can keep up.
Tax controller: homes 7 -> 4 (demand 0), shops 7 -> 4 (demand 0), factories 7 -> 3 (demand 0)
Day one (restart): dense homes with a 2x2 park in every home cell, factories, shops, coal plant, 12 river pumps, road+rail links. Audit passed.
Restarted attempt 19 on Jan 2000 after the first build landed at half scale (zoom had not taken). New plan: dense homes with parks inside every home block for land value, and a jobs-first alarm.

a20-2003 put a park on the y30 power line, cutting power to the new factory strip x110-114. Audit caught it before the clock ran. Moved the park and added a plan check that refuses parks on lines/roads.
Loan #2 (Feb 2001) and blocks 3-4: dense homes with parks, shops, factory strip x110-114.
Tax controller: homes 4 -> 5 (demand 1883), shops 4 -> 5 (demand 2000), factories 3 -> 4 (demand 59)
Jul 2002: 5,780 people - the fastest start yet, homes still in demand. Ran out of water and power, so loan #3 pays for a coal plant and 19 north riverbank pumps.

District 5 police was blocked by its own home zone and a park tile (plan clash); cleared and built it. Block 3's police (94,36) never got built for the same reason and homes now stand there; dropped it. build.py now refuses parks overlapping planned buildings.
Tax controller: homes 5 -> 6 (demand 331), shops 5 -> 6 (demand 2000), factories 4 -> 5 (demand 2000)
Turned on the four finance ordinances (+$173/yr) and City Beautification ($19/yr, raises land value - fits the tower plan).
Zoo at (110,56) in May 2003 (home demand already ~0 at 10,550 people: the recreation cap).
May 2003: 10,550 people, the fastest growth of any attempt. Turned on finance ordinances + City Beautification and built the zoo early because home demand hit zero.
Tax controller: shops 6 -> 7 (demand 2000), factories 5 -> 6 (demand 2000)
Skipped the planned home tax rise to 7% at 15,900 people: home demand is -317 and upgrades to big buildings need positive demand.
Tax controller: shops 7 -> 8 (demand 1990), factories 6 -> 7 (demand 2000)
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 9 (demand 1988), factories 7 -> 8 (demand 2000)
East homes build: roads y20/y55 and line x127 on the map edge started 4 neighbour deals ($1,000 each, $3,900 surprise). build.py now refuses edge tiles unless --edge-ok.
Tax controller: factories 8 -> 9 (demand 2000)
Tax controller: homes 6 -> 7 (demand -23)
Dec 2006: bond payments $2,599/yr vs taxes $2,095 + ordinances $306 -> about -$600/yr with $68 cash. Homes tax 6 -> 7 (home demand ~0, unemployment 2%).
Deferred the airport and second seaport to 24,000 people: cash $68 and the budget is about -$600/yr; the east factory land is still filling.
Dec 2006: 21,110 people, best year-6 of all attempts. Money is the problem: six loans cost $2,599/yr vs $2,400 income. Home tax up to 7%; airport waits until 24,000.
Big parks ($150 each, 3x3): four next to the north homes at x93-95 y1-13 - testing the home cap (+3,000 each) and land value. build.py has a new bigpark step.
Jul 2007: shop land short and home demand slightly negative with 3% unemployment - empty east home rows x123-126 y24-33 rezoned as dense shops (jobs first).
Dec 2007: 23,030 people; dense factories fill within months. New dense factory row x60-75 y70-72 facing the west homes ($578).

Jul 2008: 24,510 people, cash $205. Airport deferred again (to 28,000). Tax ceiling 10% for factories (demand ~1,900). Homes: 392 tiles in 2x2 buildings and ~100 in 3x3; mean land value 78, 134 tiles at 96+.
Jul 2008: 24,510 people. The parks are working slowly - about half the home land is now 2x2 buildings and a few towers - but money is the limit: seven loans eat almost all the tax.

Dec 2008 loan #8: stadium (101,98), east district homes x110-114 (around a pond) + dense factories x117-121. Plan left line gaps at road crossings and unjoined pipes; audit caught it before the clock ran, fixed.
Tax controller: factories 9 -> 10 (demand 1684)
Jun 2009: spare water 3% -> 7 pumps on the north lake shore x108-114 y19 ($1,785; pipes under the road/buildings cost more than estimated).
Nov 2009 loan #9: airport x106-111 y98-101 ($6,024) - shops stalled 6 months at demand +1,210 with empty land (shop cap). Second seaport still waits.
Nov 2009: 28,510 people, home demand +721 (positive again). Built the airport with loan #9 because shops had stalled for half a year.
